topics.title: Topic 1: Basic CPU Scheduling Concepts & Scheduling Criteria

questions.prompt: Which of the following events will **NOT** trigger scheduling in a non-preemptive scheduling scheme?

options.label: A
options.text: A process completes its CPU burst time

options.label: B
options.text: A process arrives on the ready queue

options.label: C
options.text: A process initiates an I/O operation

options.label: D
options.text: A process waits on a signal and blocks itself

questions.explanation: In non-preemptive scheduling, a running process only yields the CPU when it voluntarily relinquishes control (completes its burst, initiates I/O, or blocks). The arrival of a new process on the ready queue does not interrupt the running process.

questions.prompt: Which of the following time units are included in the dispatch latency during context switching between processes $P_0$ and $P_1$?

options.label: A
options.text: P0 executing

options.label: B
options.text: Save state into PCB0, and restore state from PCB1

options.label: C
options.text: P1 executing

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Dispatch latency is the overhead spent by the dispatcher to stop process $P_0$ (saving its state into $PCB_0$) and resume process $P_1$ (restoring its state from $PCB_1$). It excludes actual user-process execution time.

questions.prompt:
Consider a system running 10 I/O-bound processes and 1 CPU-bound process. Each I/O-bound process executes for 10 units of time before issuing an I/O operation (which takes 100 units). Context-switching cost is 1 unit of time.

What is the effective CPU utilization for a Round-Robin scheduler with time quantum $q = 10$?
questions.explanation:
Every execution chunk of 10 time units incurs 1 unit of context-switch overhead. The CPU spends 10 units on useful work out of every $10 + 1 = 11$ units.

$$\text{Effective Utilization} = \frac{10}{10 + 1} = \frac{10}{11} \approx 90.9\% \approx 91\%$$

questions.prompt:
Consider a system running 10 I/O-bound processes and 1 CPU-bound process. Each I/O-bound process executes for 10 units of time before issuing an I/O operation (which takes 100 units). Context-switching cost is 1 unit of time.

What is the effective CPU utilization if the time quantum is $q = 100$?
questions.explanation:
The 10 I/O-bound processes run for 10 units each before issuing I/O, each incurring 1 unit of switch cost: $10 \times (10 + 1) = 110$ units. The CPU-bound process uses the full quantum of 100 units plus 1 unit of switch cost: $100 + 1 = 101$ units.

- Useful CPU time per cycle $= 10 \times 10 + 100 = 200$.
- Elapsed time per cycle $= 110 + 101 = 211$.

$$\text{Effective Utilization} = \frac{200}{211} \approx 94.8\% \approx 94\%$$

topics.title: Topic 3: Multilevel Queue & Multilevel Feedback Queue (MLFQ)

questions.prompt: Explain the concept of multilevel queue scheduling and how it differs from multilevel feedback queue scheduling.
questions.answer:
- **Multilevel queue**: Partitions processes into fixed queues based on process type. Assignment is **permanent**, and processes cannot move between queues.
- **Multilevel feedback queue (MLFQ)**: Lets processes **move between queues** based on their execution behavior (CPU-bound vs. I/O-bound). That adapts the schedule and improves response time without requiring the burst length in advance.

questions.prompt:
Consider a 3-level feedback queue:

- $Q_0$: RR with quantum $q = 8$ ms
- $Q_1$: RR with quantum $q = 12$ ms
- $Q_2$: FCFS

Rules:

1. New processes enter $Q_0$. Higher-priority queues ($Q_0 > Q_1 > Q_2$) preempt lower ones.
2. A process that uses its full quantum in $Q_0$ moves to $Q_1$. A process that uses its full quantum in $Q_1$ moves to $Q_2$.
3. When a lower-queue process is preempted by a new arrival in $Q_0$, it returns to the **head of its current queue** with its **remaining quantum intact**.

| Process | Arrival Time (ms) | Burst Time (ms) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| $P_1$ | 0 | 12 |
| $P_2$ | 5 | 50 |
| $P_3$ | 24 | 3 |
| $P_4$ | 30 | 23 |
| $P_5$ | 33 | 26 |
| $P_6$ | 55 | 10 |

Calculate the Gantt chart, the average waiting time, and the average response time.

questions.source: 2022 Spring MC21 & 2023 Spring MC19 & 2025 Spring MC19
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is **TRUE** for Rate-Monotonic (RM) and Earliest-Deadline-First (EDF) scheduling?

options.label: A
options.text: RM uses a dynamic priority policy.

options.label: B
options.text: Both RM and EDF are non-preemptive.

options.label: C
options.text: The rationale for RM is to assign higher priority to tasks requiring CPU more often (shorter period).

options.label: D
options.text: EDF uses a static priority policy.

questions.explanation: RM uses a static priority based on period: a shorter period means a higher priority. EDF uses a dynamic priority based on deadlines. Both are preemptive.

questions.source: 2022 Fall Midterm Problem 3.3 & 2024 Spring Midterm Problem 4.2
questions.prompt:
Four periodic processes arrive at $t = 0$. Fill in the running process for timeslots $t = 0 \dots 19$ under **RM** and **EDF**, and state how many deadlines are missed.

| Process | Processing Time ($C_i$) | Deadline ($D_i$) | Period ($T_i$) | Priority in RM |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| $P_1$ | 1 | 4 | 5 | Priority 1 (highest, $T = 5$) |
| $P_2$ | 3 | 7 | 10 | Priority 3 ($T = 10$) |
| $P_3$ | 2 | 13 | 16 | Priority 4 (lowest, $T = 16$) |
| $P_4$ | 2 | 8 | 8 | Priority 2 ($T = 8$) |
questions.answer:
**Rate-monotonic** ($T_1 = 5 < T_4 = 8 < T_2 = 10 < T_3 = 16$, so $P_1 > P_4 > P_2 > P_3$)

- $t = 0..1$: $P_1$
- $t = 1..3$: $P_4$
- $t = 3..5$: $P_2$ (preempted at $t = 5$ by the next $P_1$)
- $t = 5..6$: $P_1$
- $t = 6..7$: $P_2$ finishes its third unit
- $t = 7..8$: $P_3$
- $t = 8..10$: $P_4$ (period 2)
- $t = 10..11$: $P_1$ (period 3)
- $t = 11..14$: $P_2$ (period 2)
- $t = 14..15$: $P_3$ finishes its second unit

$P_3$'s first instance arrived at $t = 0$ with deadline $13$, but it finishes at $t = 15$. **RM misses 1 deadline.**

**Earliest-deadline-first**

At $t = 0$ the absolute deadlines are $P_1: 4$, $P_2: 7$, $P_4: 8$, $P_3: 13$.

- $t = 0..1$: $P_1$
- $t = 1..4$: $P_2$
- $t = 4..6$: $P_4$
- $t = 6..7$: the next $P_1$ (deadline $5 + 4 = 9$)
- $t = 7..9$: $P_3$
- Later arrivals, including $P_4$ at $t = 8$ (deadline $16$), still meet their deadlines.

**EDF misses 0 deadlines.**
